rows.name: size
rows.reason: the frame is the logical viewport times the window's scale factor (backingScaleFactor on macOS, 1 or 2; windows and linux also give 1.25 and 1.5): a frame is compared only with one of the same viewport and scale; across scales the layout, the text and every primitive keep their size in logical px, and since task-77 phase 1b the backdrop blur and the layer blur and shadow effects too

rows.name: size
rows.reason: the canvas fills the page (100vw by 100vh) and devicePixelRatio is the scale (1 or 2 on a mac, fractional under browser zoom or a 125% or 150% display): the capture sets the desktop's viewport and scale on the page

rows.name: status-bar
rows.reason: iOS draws the status bar and the dynamic island over the app, which does not inset the gallery for the safe area; 62 pt is the top inset taken for the iPhone 17 Pro until the first capture measures it

rows.name: home-indicator
rows.reason: iOS draws the home indicator over the bottom of the app; 34 pt is the bottom inset taken until the first capture measures it

rows.name: size
rows.reason: the device's screen is the viewport and its scale the frame's (402x874 at 3x on the iPhone 17 Pro): the desktop reference is drawn at that viewport and scale

rows.name: status-bar
rows.reason: android draws the status bar over an edge-to-edge activity; 24 dp is the height taken until the first capture on the emulator measures it (a display cutout makes it taller)

rows.name: navigation-bar
rows.reason: android draws the navigation bar (gesture handle or three buttons) over the bottom of an edge-to-edge activity; 48 dp covers the three-button bar until the first capture measures it

rows.name: size
rows.reason: the device's density is the scale (420 dpi is 2.625, a fractional one) and its screen the viewport: the desktop reference is drawn at that viewport and scale
